title: Who Works in a Data Center?
summary: Many kinds of people help build, connect, power, cool, secure, and operate infrastructure.
objectives: Name several occupations connected to data centers.
Connect a broad career role to a system without treating exposure as job readiness.

vocab.def: A person who uses practical knowledge to install, maintain, or troubleshoot equipment.
The building and supporting systems that make a place work.

sections.heading: Many roles, one system
sections.body: Data Center Technicians may support equipment. Network and fiber technicians help connect systems. Electricians and mechanical professionals support power and cooling. Security, logistics, construction, facilities, and engineering teams also contribute.

sections.heading: Different strengths matter
sections.body: Some roles involve tools and troubleshooting. Others involve planning, safety, communication, documentation, or protecting information. No single job does everything.

sections.heading: Explore, do not decide today
sections.body: Sixth grade is a time to notice what interests you. You do not need to choose a career or prove a job skill now.

practice.prompt: Match a problem to a possible team: a broken connection, a temperature concern, or a delivery of equipment.

quiz.question: Why are many types of workers involved?
options: Different systems need different knowledge and responsibilities
Only one person can work in a data center
quiz.answer: Different systems need different knowledge and responsibilities

reflectionPrompt: Which kind of work would you like to learn more about, and why?
